title: A Glasshouse for the Aftermath
premise: Sebastian Marchetti has spent eleven years writing postcards to his sister Lucia at an address that burned down the night she disappeared — letters he pretends are a harmless ritual. When a demolition crew uncovers a tin box of undelivered letters behind a wardrobe in the old Marchetti glasshouse, Sebastian learns someone else was answering Lucia all along, and that her disappearance was witnessed, paid for, and buried by the family that employed them both. Returning to the decaying estate where his sister once worked, Sebastian must decode Lucia's coded correspondence, confront the matriarch who orchestrated the cover-up, and choose between the comfortable lie of survival and the ruinous truth. In the end, Sebastian burns the glasshouse himself — not to erase the past, but to give his sister's words somewhere to go.
about_author: Astrid Amberdale is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the correspondence of families too proud to burn their letters and too ashamed to read them. She writes from a converted potting shed on the Sussex coast, where the glass is original and the memories are not.

chapters.title: The Smile That Ends Conversations
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. We meet him in a coastal town, writing his weekly postcard to a burned-down address, deflecting a neighbor's kindness with his practiced smile. The chapter establishes his ritualized grief and isolation. Emotional beat: the quiet horror of a life built around an absence no one is allowed to mention.

chapters.title: Behind the Wardrobe
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A demolition notice arrives for the old Marchetti glasshouse; a former groundskeeper's son delivers a tin box found in the wall — forty undelivered letters, all addressed to Lucia, all in a hand Sebastian almost recognizes. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into compulsion as the ritual is violently interrupted.

chapters.title: Letters in a Hand I Knew
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, with interpolated letter fragments. He reads the first letters: warm, coded, signed only 'G.' The letters reference a greenhouse, a payment, a night in November. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing his private grief was shared by a stranger all along.

chapters.title: The Glasshouse on the Estate Map
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He researches the Vane family who owned the estate, finding Lucia listed as a gardener's assistant — and finding a fire report dated three days after her last letter. Emotional beat: suspicion crystallizing; the past begins to feel engineered.

chapters.title: What the Groundskeeper's Son Remembers
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV (first of his alternating chapters). Tomas, who found the box, recalls his father drinking himself silent after the fire and whispering about 'what Mrs. Vane bought that autumn.' Emotional beat: inherited fear, the price children pay for parents' silence.

chapters.title: The Return Ticket
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Against every instinct, he packs Lucia's unsent replies — which he has kept hidden for eleven years — and takes the train to the valley. Emotional beat: terror disguised as resolve; leaving the life that protected him.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot on Purpose
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The village is prosperous, polite, and curiously blank about the Vanes. A pub landlady serves him a free meal and warns him off the estate with a smile he recognizes — his own smile, learned from somewhere. Emotional beat: the uncanny recognition that his survival strategies were taught, not chosen.

chapters.title: Mrs. Vane Receives
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He gains entry to the estate under pretense of buying salvaged glass and meets the matriarch, aged but razor-sharp, who identifies him within minutes as 'the Marchetti boy.' Emotional beat: the thrill and sickness of standing in front of the person his nightmares were modeled on.

chapters.title: G., Full Name Given
chapters.summary: Lucia's letters, read in Sebastian's POV. The correspondent was Gideon Vane, the son — Lucia's secret ally and lover, whose letters stopped the week of the fire. Emotional beat: grief complicated by betrayal; Lucia had a whole life Sebastian never knew.

chapters.title: Tomas Opens His Father's Trunk
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas finds his father's ledger: dates, sums, and the word 'witnessed' beside the fire date — his father was paid to be elsewhere, and to stay elsewhere. Emotional beat: the crushing discovery that silence was a salary.

chapters.title: The Conservatory of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian and Gideon Vane — now a broken, half-forgotten man living in a converted orangery — meet. Gideon confirms Lucia planned to expose the family's forged land deeds and was given a choice: leave quietly or be erased. Emotional beat: two survivors circling the same wound from opposite sides.

chapters.title: The Choice They Made for Her
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Flashback to the November night: Mrs. Vane confronted Lucia; Gideon chose his inheritance over her, believing the lie that she'd be paid and safe. Emotional beat: guilt as a slow poison; complicity dressed as love.

chapters.title: Ledger, Ash, Ledger
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Mrs. Vane's lawyer visits Tomas with a settlement offer — money for the box, for silence, for the ledger. Tomas refuses, then finds his own name already in an older page of the ledger: paid, as a boy, to forget. Emotional beat: the horror that corruption reaches backward through time.

chapters.title: The Coded Garden
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Deciphering Lucia's horticultural ciphers with Gideon's help, Sebastian learns she hid the deed evidence in the glasshouse itself — in the roots of an heirloom fig, in the seed archive. Emotional beat: hope rekindled; his sister was always three moves ahead.

chapters.title: Mrs. Vane's Version
chapters.summary: Mrs. Vane's POV. The matriarch, lucid and unrepentant, narrates her own justification: the family, the valley, the jobs — everything balanced against one inconvenient gardener's girl. Emotional beat: chilling clarity; power explaining itself without apology.

chapters.title: The Fire, Retold
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas's father, dying, finally speaks: the fire was set to destroy Lucia's evidence, with Lucia inside or near it — no one stayed to check, because checking was not in the contract. Emotional beat: the truth landing like a verdict; survival revealed as a purchased cowardice.

chapters.title: Excavation
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. With Tomas and Gideon, Sebastian digs the fig's roots and opens the seed archive: the deeds, the confession Lucia wrote the night she died, addressed to 'my brother, who will smile and say nothing.' Emotional beat: devastating intimacy — she knew exactly who he would become.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Mrs. Vane makes her final offer: everything, the estate itself, in exchange for the archive and silence. Sebastian, for the first time, uses the smile — and declines. Emotional beat: the smile turned into a weapon; the price of survival refused.

chapters.title: What Gideon Owes
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon publicly signs a statement corroborating the archive, forfeiting his inheritance and his mother's protection, choosing Lucia's truth over the family name at last. Emotional beat: redemption arriving too late to be clean, but arriving.

chapters.title: The Burning of the Glasshouse
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, climax. Before the lawyers and the valley can bury it again, Sebastian sets the glasshouse alight — a controlled, witnessed burning, the archive already copied and sent to a journalist and the county records. Emotional beat: fire reclaimed from the people who used it first; grief given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: Postcards, Forward Address
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Months later: the Vanes' empire under investigation, Tomas tending the replanted fig, Gideon planting Lucia's seed archive in the ruined glasshouse's footprint. Sebastian writes one last postcard — to Lucia, care of the new orchard. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into tending.

chapters.title: A Glasshouse for the Aftermath
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, closing. At the first spring opening of the Lucia Marchetti Memorial Glass, built from salvaged panes, Sebastian smiles at a stranger — and this time the smile begins a conversation. He tells her the whole story. Emotional beat: the price of survival finally paid in full, and worth it; memory planted, not buried.
